Show the structure of a scale

Source: R/str.R
str.NestedScale.Rd

Prints the tree of scale_tree(): the properties of the object, the columns of its leaftable and what a subclass adds, each with its size and whether it is fixed, derived or mutable. The properties themselves are read with @ or S7::prop(); S7::prop_names() gives their names.

# S3 method for class 'NestedScale'
str(object, ...)

# S3 method for class '`nestedscales::NestedScale`'
str(object, ...)

# S3 method for class '`nestedscales::ScaleProduct`'
str(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A NestedScale or a ScaleProduct.

...

Passed to the print method of scale_tree().

Value

object, invisibly.

See also

scale_tree()

Examples

str(scale_example())
#> <NestedScale> example@491e9cf6
#> ├─ leaftable   data.frame [7 x 6]            one row per atom
#> │  ├─ unit     key                  fixed
#> │  ├─ sector   frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ class    frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ group    frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ size     weight               mutable
#> │  └─ count    weight               mutable
#> ├─ frames      chr [4]              fixed    sector, class, group, unit
#> ├─ members     list [4]             derived  from leaftable: sector 2, class 3, group 3, unit 7
#> ├─ key         chr [1]              fixed    unit
#> ├─ meta        list [4]             mutable  name, desc, weights, default_weight
#> ├─ attributes  data.frame [0 x 10]  mutable  attach_attributes_scale()
#> ├─ aliases     data.frame [0 x 4]   mutable  attach_aliases_scale()
#> └─ labels      data.frame [0 x 4]   mutable  attach_labels_scale()
S7::prop_names(scale_example())
#> [1] "leaftable"  "frames"     "members"    "key"        "meta"      
#> [6] "attributes" "aliases"    "labels"
